title: Prove exact tensor splitting feasibility for every cap (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. For finite positive-integer paid and target inventories, real `0<t<1`, and positive integer cap base `c`, tensoring and disjoint capped splitting beat the unchanged target moment at some positive power exactly when

```text
max(P_t, P_1 c^(t-1)) < T_t.
lim_(v->infinity) S_v^(1/v) = max(P_t, P_1 c^(t-1)).
```

`S_v` is the optimal charge over every partition of each tensor job into integer pieces at most `c^v`. Equality in either necessary inequality blocks every power. If the least target rank is `k>=2`, some integer cap below it works exactly when `P_t<T_t` and `P_1 (k-1)^(t-1)<T_t`. The proof uses a two-sided charge bound, finite product moments and a squeeze argument.

This adds only `research/split-only-tensor-feasibility/`. No target completion, cross-job merging, new kappa or native supplier is claimed. The selected frontier is unchanged. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19595330).

Credit zxv #4433 for the splitting framework, 1337isnot1337 #4412/#4414/#4416 for chronological product/completion, and jacobalansussman for the compiler, and their retained native/helper/controller/outer lineage. The elementary concavity/product arguments are classical. The new result is the exact tensor feasibility screen and strict boundary. Prior one-job coefficient and net-tax results are background, not proof inputs or replay targets.

## Evidence

The abstract fixture `T={4,4,4}, P={9}, t=1/2` has raw moment and rank-one surpluses both equal to three. The new bound excludes cap base two at every power despite those surpluses. Base three passes. A separate exact fixture has first-power equality nine and a second-power charge of 73 below target 81, protecting the distinction between eventual and immediate gain.

Local CPython 3.12.15 normal and optimized checks pass at `06c46bed7ec9168c9d0b2a5561eeb6079b0f1ef1`:

- 18,432 one-job splits; 256 exact arbitrary-partition DP optima; 468 tensor histograms; 2,496 feasibility cases, including 1,767 actually evaluated sufficient-power witnesses through power twenty.
- 3,072 independently enumerated ordered job tuples, 176 literal partition contexts, 39 boundary checks and fifteen rejected invalid inputs. All arithmetic uses integers and rational root brackets.
- Both registered commands, metadata/source pins, exact committed bytes/modes and declared source ancestry pass. Each direct command takes under one second locally; the registered pair completes in under two seconds. These are replay-budget observations, not speedup claims.
- Official six-file export integrity passes. Normal and optimized replay from a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH reproduce the complete output; all seven exported files, including the manifest, retain their bytes and modes. Five disposable scientific mutations reject in both modes.

Reproduce from the repository root; another CPython 3.12 path may replace this interpreter:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/split-only-tensor-feasibility/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/split-only-tensor-feasibility/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/split-only-tensor-feasibility
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/split-only-tensor-feasibility --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Expected markers include `PASS_SPLIT_ONLY_TENSOR_FEASIBILITY`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Direct replay writes nothing and generates a receipt bound to all package hashes. No predecessor scientific executable was replayed.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The all-real/all-power conclusion rests on the written proof. Finite checks corroborate it. The inventory model permits only within-job disjoint partitions and retains all targets unchanged. Completion, cross-job merging, target debits and additional charges need new analysis. Native realization, arbitrary-input physical delivery, owned restoration, chronological closure, compiler, precision, stock, tape and outer recovery remain unproved or unpriced here. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No selected cold replay, native suite, Lean or Docker run was performed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Can one changed native inventory pass the screen with cap `min(target)-1` and avoid target completion? Start with its complete arbitrary-input tensor/splitting contract and full physical bill.
- What is the exact any-power criterion when same-owner target completion is allowed? Both target credit and paid completion costs must remain in a new two-sided estimate.

## Related open work

- [#7135](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7135) optimizes the quotient staircase of the distinct one-job net splitting tax. This proves a whole-inventory exponential rate and any-power criterion without using that optimizer; no common numerical optimum is recomputed.

- [#7532](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7532) proves a sharp separated source-count floor from inventory summaries. This result concerns paid-moment feasibility under capped tensor splitting; no common numerical quantity is compared.

The completion refresh read this account's seven other open PRs created since the CLAIM. Only #7532 adds adjacent compiler accounting; none studies the same fixed-cap feasibility criterion or gives a conflicting common number. No extra computation checked another contribution. Main README/proof and merged-PR searches supplement the sparse cache. Arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain outside that coverage.

## CI notes

CI did not certify this package. At unchanged head `06c46bed7ec9168c9d0b2a5561eeb6079b0f1ef1`, [run 43468242577](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43468242577) failed in [plan job 132033028843](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43468242577/job/132033028843), step `Onboarding helper tests`. I read the checks once and downloaded the job log. It reports exactly one failing test out of 760, with 24 skipped:

`test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`

The AssertionError states that `` `make frontier7000-verify` `` was not found in the CI verification document. On unchanged main/base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, `certificates/selected-result.json` names that command, while `docs/ci-verification.md` still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. I confirmed both base-file contents. This PR changes neither file nor the failing test. The [package replay job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43468242577/job/132035846661) was skipped because plan failed.

I also downloaded and read the plan logs for [run 42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314/job/130140894651), [run 42903313790](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790/job/130134720799), and [run 43468190113](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43468190113/job/132032847132). Each reports the identical failing test and missing-command assertion, 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped. Their replay jobs were also skipped. These observations confirm the shared repository-level navigation failure; they provide no scientific certification of this package.

All claimed scientific checks remain local. No fix, retrigger commit or CI rerun was made, and the published head is unchanged. Every registered package command passed locally; independent scientific acceptance remains unclaimed.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: one isolated opt-in research package. No shared checker, frozen predecessor, selected record or frontier change.
